title: Console MVP: Essential Route Set + Degraded-Mode UX for Dashboards/Traces/Cost
creator: Sofia Park
description:
Scope decision and acceptance criteria for a reduced Console MVP surface that targets three high-value telemetry features: per-route dashboards, trace sampling surface, and a lightweight cost breakdown. Goal: ship a deterministic, debuggable experience that delivers core customer value while meeting delivery constraints for Q1. This ticket defines the 'Essential Route Set' (ERS) approach, the degraded-mode UX that replaces full-featured cards when backend data or ingestion is limited, and the exact acceptance criteria for launch.

Context: previous scopes attempted an expansive tile set and deep trace exploration UI which pushed infra and analytics deadlines. We must de-scope interactive deep trace timelines, multi-card drilldowns, and long-term storage retention options until a follow-up release. Instead, the ERS will surface: top 10 routes by request volume, a single aggregated latency card per route, sampled trace links with open-instrumented viewer fallback, and a tokenized cost histogram for the selected time window.

Tradeoffs and rationale:
- Remove rich trace flamegraph interactions to avoid additional backend indexing and reduce query cost; users still get trace links and span-level links that open in the full tracer when available.
- Limit dashboards to ERS to reduce cardinality on metrics ingest and simplify routing policies; long tail routes are accessible via a CSV export or the logs view (follow-up).
- Implement degraded-mode UI that explicitly indicates partial data and surfaces a CTA to retry or view raw logs, preventing silent failures.

Operational constraints:
- Backend will rely on a simplified metrics pipeline (1m rollup) and limited retention (30d) for MVP. Any change to retention or sampling requires a separate capacity and billing approval.

Deliverables and artifacts:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/ERS+MVP+PRD (design + acceptance)
- Design sketches: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/console-ers-mvp-sketches (dashboard + degraded states)
- Engineering epic: ENG-8421 (metrics pipeline), ENG-8513 (trace link glue), ENG-8577 (cost histogram)
acceptance_criteria: ERS routes list displays top 10 routes by 24h request volume and updates within 120s of pipeline ingest
Each ERS route shows a single aggregated latency card (p50/p95) with 30d retention; cards have clear stale-data indicators
Trace links for sampled requests open the standard tracer viewer; if tracer unavailable show descriptive fallback modal with raw-span preview
Cost histogram renders for selected time window (24h, 7d, 30d) and matches billing-reconciled sample within 5% for top 10 routes
Degraded-mode UI appears whenever metrics ingestion latency exceeds 3x SLO or data is missing; CTA offers retry and raw-logs link
Telemetry instrumentation includes observability for card render latency, query error rate, and degraded-mode hit rate (dashboarded)
Docs: Quickstart and Known Limitations published (console/docs/ers-mvp-quickstart) and linked from console onboarding
E2E smoke test exists that validates ERS cards render for a synthetic workload and trace link resolves (automated in CI)
comments: 2025-11-12 - PM sync: agreed ERS reduces scope by ~60% vs earlier plan; engineering to confirm pipeline ops cost delta.
2025-11-18 - Eng update (R. Menon): metric rollup prototype returns within 90s for 1k routes; will limit front-end query to top 10 to bound cost.
2025-11-25 - Design review: replaced multi-card drilldown with single expand-to-modal pattern to keep UI predictable on small screens.
2025-11-30 - Security review note: no customer PII surfaced in ERS cards. KMS integration not required for MVP (revisit for exports).
2025-12-02 - Stakeholder approval: Growth and Support signed off on customer-facing limitations doc and the degraded-mode messaging copy. Next: schedule canary for internal teams.
Follow-ups: define export contract for long-tail routes (PM-100101) and trace deep-dive roadmap (PM-100102).
